name: The right fields, the right types, and nothing extra
description: A stricter contract than shape alone. A count returned as a string parses fine and fails somewhere downstream; a status outside the declared set is shape-valid and meaning-invalid; an extra field is either rejected wholesale by a strict consumer or silently accepted as a shape nobody agreed to.
goal: Read the account file and produce an artifact named 'report' matching the schema below. 'status' must be one of 'open', 'closed' or 'on-hold' exactly. 'open_items' must be a number, not a string. Do not add fields the schema does not declare, however useful they seem.

output_contract.description: An object with 'account', 'status', 'open_items' and 'notes', matching the schema below.

files.content: Northstar. The account is open. Three items remain outstanding: the renewal signature, region three staffing, and the integration sign-off.

assertions.description: The subject chose to finish. The file says everything the report needs, so stopping to ask fails here
Only the declared fields are present. A strict consumer rejects the whole payload over an extra one; a lenient one accepts a shape nobody agreed to
A count returned as a string parses, propagates, and fails somewhere that has forgotten where it came from
Shape-valid and meaning-invalid is the case a schema check alone passes, so the set is graded separately from the type

coverage.note: Three cells, three assertions, three paths. Graded separately rather than by one schema check over the whole object, because a single conforms_to would report the first violation it met and the three failures would be indistinguishable in the evidence.
